$comment: The work queue. Agents pull from here; the orchestrator sets owner and status. Phases run in order; tasks within a phase run in parallel on disjoint paths.

tasks.notes: Two manifest amendments applied: hash split out of rng, assert renamed guard (validators return their argument). Colour maths ruled into draw, not core. Two-tier determinism rule adopted into AGENTS.md and enforced by lint via @tier-b markers. Found the replay gap — routed to persist.

tasks.notes: Tile size fixed at 64x32 (any other size is exactly a camera zoom). Three tilemap storages behind one TileSource so pathfinding cannot tell them apart. A* AND flow fields. Path reframed as a curve sampled by arc length — the demo crowd collapses to one expression. Elevation on vertices. Took the tap-to-tile maths, Rect, and the anchor primitive.

CatchUp.fromSeconds is REQUIRED, not optional — advanceOver and solveCrossingOver must resume a partially consumed absence without restarting the warp. A crossing is a phase boundary, discovered rather than scheduled; re-entering with a fresh span pays for K absences instead of one, and each restart is cheaper, so the exploit climbs back in through the function that closes it.

OfflineCurve.uncappedSeconds documented as a design constraint: if a standing charge accrues on a cycle, U must exceed that cycle period by a wide margin or the cycle is skippable. The designer meets this at the field they are picking a number for.
tasks.notes: From D2. Also: the demo picked exponent 0.625 rather than 0.6 because 5/8 is dyadic, making credited time Tier A via a sqrt chain instead of pow. Check whether the default curve should do the same.

tasks.title: Fix the night-tab exploit the sim architect found
acceptance: a time warp discounts standing charges as well as income, so LAMP ROAD currently rewards closing the tab during the night
decide whether oil burn is exempt from the warp, or the design changes
whichever it is, the reason is written into the demo RFC
tasks.notes: Refused the exemption: it would mean two ledgers and two anchors, and would make oil(t) non-polynomial so solveCrossingOver no longer applies. Moved the pressure from flow to state instead — a guttered lamp stays out until tapped. Closing the tab is never a win, and the mechanism that makes it a loss is the game thesis evaluated while the player was away.
